newsitem.title: FRANCE: Rebel spokesman threatens France over Mobutu.
newsitem.headline: Rebel spokesman threatens France over Mobutu.

text.p: The spokesman in Paris for Zaire's new rulers on Sunday threatened to "plant bombs" in France if it gives exile shelter to Mobutu Sese Seko and demanded that the ousted president's property in the country be handed over.

"If Mobutu comes into exile in France, we will start planting bombs," an infuriated N'Zamba Afri Ku-Nyeng told reporters outside the Zairean embassy in Paris after police prevented him and supporters from taking over the building.
"If France accepts Mobutu, it will have to deal with all the Congolese people," said Ku-Nyeng, who had earlier vowed to hunt Mobutu "wherever he goes" in exile.
"France must do everything so that we can recover everything Mobutu owns in France, apartments, villas and bank accounts," he said.
Despite animated arguments, the protest outside the Zairean embasy was not violent.

Mobutu owns a palatial mansion in the posh French Riviera resort of Roquebrune Cap Martin, near Nice, where he made several stays to recover from cancer surgery over the past few months while Laurent Kabila's rebels were gradually taking over the country he ruled.
There has been speculation that Mobutu may come into exile to France, which supported long after other western countries had dropped him.

But French foreign ministry officials say they are unaware of his whereabouts and plans. Commentators say that Paris is unlikely to offer him shelter, at least before a May 25-June 1 parliamentary election, for fear that his presence would be a campaign issue.

A friend in Paris of the Mobutu family said the ousted president, earlier reported to have fled into exile in Morocco after the rebels overran Kinshasa, was still in his home village of Gbadolite in northern Zaire on Sunday morning.
The man, who asked not to be named, told Reuters he had been in touch by satellite telephone with children of Mobutu in Gbadolite at 10 a.m. (0800 GMT) who told him he was in a meeting.
He said later attempts to speak to Gbadolite had failed.
